lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: applying the rules to real risk and screening questions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: P(delay | rain) = P(delay). What does that mean?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A box holds 11 items, of which 8 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 14/100 and P(B) = 37/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 27/100, P(B) = 16/100, and P(A and B) = 11/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.

items.prompt: A box holds 17 items, of which 4 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 29/100 and P(B) = 53/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 16/100, P(B) = 16/100, and P(A and B) = 13/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
